models.title: Time-series plots
models.summary: Compare selected series over their actual observed sample.
assumptions: Series units and transformations must be comparable before sharing an axis.
models.label: Descriptive

models.title: Correlation and rolling correlation
models.summary: Describe contemporaneous co-movement and its change across trailing windows.
assumptions: Correlation describes association; it does not identify a causal effect.
All pairs use the same complete sample.
models.label: Descriptive

models.title: Country comparison and ranking
models.summary: Rank country averages or latest observations over explicitly recorded samples.
assumptions: Cross-country series must have comparable definitions and units.
Unequal country samples can change rankings.
models.label: Descriptive

models.title: Unit-root and stationarity tests
models.summary: Compare ADF and Phillips-Perron unit-root tests with the KPSS stationarity test.
assumptions: The deterministic trend specification must match the series.
ADF and PP have a unit-root null; KPSS has a stationarity null.
Tests have limited power in short or structurally changing samples.
models.label: Descriptive

models.title: Linear regression
models.summary: Estimate a conditional linear association with HAC or HC1 uncertainty.
assumptions: Regressors are exogenous for the conditional mean.
HAC allows weak serial dependence and heteroskedasticity; HC1 does not correct serial dependence.
Coefficient intervals use Student t reference quantiles and do not establish causation.
models.label: Association, not causation

models.title: Autoregressive distributed lag regression
models.summary: Estimate lagged responses and show their equivalent error-correction parameterisation.
assumptions: Conditional errors are not correlated with included regressors and lagged outcomes.
The error-correction form is algebraic; it does not by itself establish cointegration.
Selected regressors include current values and every lag through the chosen order.
models.label: Association, not causation

models.title: Rolling and recursive regression
models.summary: Track coefficient estimates in trailing windows or an expanding historical sample.
assumptions: Regressors are exogenous for the conditional mean.
HAC allows weak serial dependence and heteroskedasticity; HC1 does not correct serial dependence.
Coefficient intervals use Student t reference quantiles and do not establish causation.
Each window uses only observations available through its endpoint.
Pointwise bands do not adjust for comparisons across many windows.
models.label: Association, not causation

models.title: Granger predictive-content test
models.summary: Test whether lagged values of one series help predict another, conditional on its own lags.
assumptions: The bivariate lag regression is correctly specified and covariance-stationary.
The classical SSR F test assumes homoskedastic uncorrelated errors.
The test measures predictive content, not causation.
models.label: Descriptive

models.title: Hodrick-Prescott filter
models.summary: Separate a smooth trend from a cycle using an explicit smoothing penalty.
assumptions: The smoothing penalty determines the trend-cycle split.
This two-sided filter uses future observations and has endpoint bias; it is not a real-time forecast.
models.label: Descriptive

models.title: Hamilton regression filter
models.summary: Define the cycle as the error in a long-horizon projection on past observations.
assumptions: The specified projection horizon and lag count define the cycle.
Full-sample coefficients use future information; this is a descriptive filter, not a real-time forecast.
models.label: Descriptive

references.title: Hamilton (2018), Why You Should Never Use the Hodrick-Prescott Filter

models.title: Vector autoregression
models.summary: Estimate joint dynamics and, with recursive assumptions, responses to a chosen shock.
assumptions: The chosen lag structure and deterministic terms describe the joint dynamics.
Innovations are serially uncorrelated; the bootstrap assumes exchangeable innovations.
Exogenous regressors are treated as fixed and contemporaneously exogenous.
models.label: Association, not causation

references.title: Lütkepohl (2005), New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis

models.title: Recursive identification
models.summary: Identify ordered shocks with Cholesky restrictions and explicit shock units.
assumptions: The chosen lag structure and deterministic terms describe the joint dynamics.
Innovations are serially uncorrelated; the bootstrap assumes exchangeable innovations.
Exogenous regressors are treated as fixed and contemporaneously exogenous.
Earlier variables do not respond contemporaneously to later shocks in the stated ordering.
models.label: Model-based scenario, not a forecast

references.title: Lütkepohl (2005), New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis

models.title: Local projections
models.summary: Estimate a separate response at each horizon with explicit controls and samples.
assumptions: Impulse exogeneity is required for a causal interpretation.
HAC inference is asymptotic; intervals are pointwise.
models.label: Conditional association, unless an identified shock is supplied

references.title: Jordà (2005), Estimation and Inference of Impulse Responses by Local Projections
Montiel Olea and Plagborg-Møller (2021), Local Projection Inference Is Simpler and More Robust Than You Think

models.title: Historical decomposition
models.summary: Account for past movements under an explicitly ordered stable recursive VAR.
assumptions: The chosen lag structure and deterministic terms describe the joint dynamics.
Innovations are serially uncorrelated; the bootstrap assumes exchangeable innovations.
Exogenous regressors are treated as fixed and contemporaneously exogenous.
models.label: Model-based accounting of the past under the recursive identification, not evidence of what caused each movement.

references.title: Lütkepohl (2005), New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis

models.title: Reusable identified shock
models.summary: Expose dated orthogonalised residuals from a first-stage recursive VAR.
assumptions: The chosen lag structure and deterministic terms describe the joint dynamics.
Innovations are serially uncorrelated; the bootstrap assumes exchangeable innovations.
Exogenous regressors are treated as fixed and contemporaneously exogenous.
models.label: Generated shock; conditional on the stated recursive identification

references.title: Lütkepohl (2005), New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis

models.title: Common-shock country comparison
models.summary: Reuse one identified shock in country-specific LPs and show actual samples.
assumptions: Impulse exogeneity is required for a causal interpretation.
HAC inference is asymptotic; intervals are pointwise.
models.label: Conditional association, unless an identified shock is supplied

references.title: Jordà (2005), Estimation and Inference of Impulse Responses by Local Projections
Montiel Olea and Plagborg-Møller (2021), Local Projection Inference Is Simpler and More Robust Than You Think
